extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent attorneys, and patent applicants (practitioners interested in 1878 U.S. patent office procedures)
extracted.subtask_short: US patent examination and issuance procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the U.S. Patent Office's procedures, standards, and recordkeeping for examination, amendment, appeals, interferences, and the preparation and issuance of patents (1878). Useful for examiners and practitioners to understand filing, prosecution, and issuance steps and criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner search and examination effort
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires a critical reading of the specification and a search through descriptions of prior inventions pertaining to the same subject found in the specifications and drawings of domestic and foreign patents, and in other printed publications, or in manuscript digests of the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such search is more or less extended according to the complexity of the invention and the antiquity of the art to which it pertains. It frequently requires, in single cases, the inspection of many hundred drawings and extended reading, occupying several days' time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance prerequisite — patentability and description
rubrics_metrics.description: If upon examination it appears that the matter specified is patentable, and that it is well and sufficiently described, and that it is particularly and distinctly pointed out in the claim, the application is allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: About fifteen per cent of completed applications are, after examination, allowed without objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection notice and guidance to applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application is rejected, the Commissioner of Patents, by the Examiner, causes the applicant to be informed of the reasons of such rejection, and to be furnished with pertinent information for his guidance as to the further prosecution of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the applicant with reasons and guidance enabling response or amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant response to rejection — reconsideration and amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may respond to such rejection by a request for reconsideration with or without amendment of his specification, and he may ask a reconsideration as often as new references are cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In most applications there occur one, two, or more rejections; repeated reconsideration requests are permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: File recordkeeping of communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Every official communication by the Examiner in an application, and every communication from the applicant or his attorney, is placed in the file and noted upon the back of the file-wrapper in proper order and time, and said wrapper exhibits a complete index of the history of the case from the date of its receipt in the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every official action by the Examiner is duly noted in his register adjacent to the original entry of the application, and all official letters are copied by press into a letter-book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written amendment entry procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Written amendments of a specification are entered as follows: Matter to be inserted is inclosed by lines on the amendment, and the place of insertion, as stated by applicant, marked on the body of the specification. Matter to be erased from the specification is inclosed by lines and canceled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar reference letters are placed on the amendment and on the specification at the place where it is to be entered, and said letters are indorsed on the back of the amendment. Red ink is used for distinctness. Amendments are made in a large majority of cases and may be numerous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation of prosecution correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: The correspondence, including rejections and amendments, is continued until the application is put in condition for allowance, or its further prosecution is neglected, or an appeal is taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory bars and appeal route
rubrics_metrics.description: If any one of the statutory bars to the grant of a patent ... is found to exist upon examination by the Primary Examiner, and the finding is adhered to upon re-examination, then an appeal may be taken from such adverse decision to the Board of Examiners-in-Chief, and from an adverse decision of the Board to the Commissioner in person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites sections and rules as authority for appeal steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference adverse finding appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party to an interference, against whom an adverse finding of priority has been rendered, may appeal from the judgment of the Examiner of Interferences to the Board of Examiners-in-Chief, and from an adverse decision of the Board to the Commissioner in person.

rubrics_metrics.name: General appeals to the Commissioner
rubrics_metrics.description: Every other question or dispute, under any section of the law or rules, raised before any tribunal having cognizance of the subject-matter ... is appealable, after adverse decision, directly to the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to Primary Examiner, Examiner of Trade-Marks, Examiner of Interferences, Board of Examiners-in-Chief, or heads of divisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal filing and processing procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of an appeal is recorded in the Application-room, and the written reasons of appeal placed in a file-wrapper and sent to the proper Examiner, who makes written answer to the same and sends the application and the appeal-file containing reasons and answer to the clerk in charge of appeal-files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After final adjudication by the Board or Commissioner or Supreme Court, the application, appeal papers, and decision are returned to the Examiner, who allows the application with or without amendment, or files it among rejected cases according to the tenor of said decision, and sends the appeal-file to the clerk in charge of appeal and interference files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interlocutory appeals to Commissioner handled within application-file
rubrics_metrics.description: In an appeal to the Commissioner in an interlocutory matter no separate file is kept, but the reasons and answer are inserted in the application-file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay policy during interference proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: When an interference is found to exist between two or more cases the applications are delayed, if practicable without injustice, until each is put in condition for allowance in case it receives award of priority of invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One application at least, claiming the interfering matter, must be in such condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference notification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon declaration of preliminary interference by the Examiner the several parties or their attorneys, and, in case of a patent, both the patentee and his attorney of record, and all assignees, are notified of the interference, of the names of the parties to the same and their attorneys, and of the residences of both, and of the interfering subject-matter, and of the claims in each case embracing such matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of these are made in the letter-book, and also written copies to be sent to the parties, and the proper entries are made in the register and on the file-wrappers, and the files and papers sent to the Examiner of Interferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference preliminary statement timing and mailing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Examiner of Interferences, if the interference appears to have been declared in proper form, fixes the time of filing preliminary statements therein, and causes the copies of letters furnished him to be mailed to the appropriate parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return for correction if rules not complied with
rubrics_metrics.description: If ... he finds on inspection that official rules have not been complied with in the preliminary declaration by the Examiner, he returns the same for correction, in which event a new declaration ... is usually necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures procedural compliance before interference proceeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference-file preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Interference-files are prepared by the clerk in charge, as in case of an application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-interference disposition of files
rubrics_metrics.description: After decision by the Examiner of Interferences as to priority, upon evidence and argument, or after final adjudication upon appeal to the Commissioner, the files and papers are returned to the Examiner, who sends the application of the successful party to issue, unless such party is already a patentee or had neglected to properly amend his application before declaration, or unless an interference with a subsequent application occurs, or ... evidence was incidentally elicited ... which makes it necessary that the application be rejected for want of patentability of subject-matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to reconsideration and appeal after interference-related rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: In the latter event the applicant is entitled to a reconsideration and an appeal in the usual course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of interference and rejected files
rubrics_metrics.description: Interference-files are returned to the proper clerk, and the rejected cases placed among rejected files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention period for rejected and forfeited files
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejected cases that are not prosecuted are retained for two years in the Examiner's room, and forfeited cases that are not renewed are held eighteen months. Both are finally sent to the Draftsman's division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storage of examined/allowed cases pending final fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Examined or allowed cases are kept in the Issue-division until payment of the final fee, or until forfeiture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If final fee received, case sent to Drafting-division; if forfeited, returned to Examiner. A record of forfeited cases is kept in the Issue-division, and also of allowed cases temporarily returned to the Examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal of forfeited cases procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: In the renewal of forfeited cases the original file and papers are usually retained, the renewal fee and the new date being noted (from Application-room) upon the original file-wrapper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation for issue — Examiner's duties
rubrics_metrics.description: An application having been found to possess the proper requisites is made ready for issue by the Examiner. A brief of the invention is inserted in the file. The name of the applicant, title of invention, and date of allowance are noted upon the face of the drawing, and also the removal of the model, which latter is sent to the Model-room and retained in secrecy until after the grant of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The title is also indorsed upon the file-wrapper, and the date of examination and Examiner's signature placed upon the face of the same.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading and error correction before drafting
rubrics_metrics.description: The file and drawing are now sent to the proof-readers in the Issue-division, who inspect or edit the specification and drawing, and if material errors are discovered return the same to the Examiner for correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting-division recording and portfolio handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Immediately after the case is edited it is sent to the Drafting-division, where the name of the patentee, the title of the invention, and the name of the Examiner who passed the case are recorded, the date of issue is written upon the file, and the drawing is placed in the 'Issue-portfolio.' The file is then sent to the Issue-division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue-division finalization and allowance notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon its receipt in the Issue-division it receives the signature of the chief clerk, a circular of allowance is mailed to the proper party, and the file is pigeon-holed to await the payment of the final fee, which, when received, is noted upon the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alphabetical Register entry requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Issue-division the case is dated and numbered, and an entry is made on the Alphabetical Register of Patentees, which register shows a list of all patentees, alphabetically arranged, the title of the invention, the class to which it belongs, the date and number of the patent, and the name and address of the person to whom the patent is to be sent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent-Head Book and number assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: The case is next entered on the Patent-Head Book, and the file then sent to the Drafting-division. The drawing belonging to the case is taken from the Issue-portfolio, and the prospective number of the patent is indorsed upon it. The brief is removed from the file ... and the number of the patent is in like manner indorsed upon the latter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final pre-print examination before Public Printer
rubrics_metrics.description: The file is returned to the Issue-division, where it receives an examination to insure that it is in proper condition to go forward, and is delivered by messenger to the Public Printer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and printing proofs procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification is put in type at the Government Printing Office, and the file, with a proof of the specification, is returned to the Issue-division, where it is revised and returned to the Printer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'notice of patent,' giving the prospective number and date of the patent, is next made out in the same division and mailed to the person entitled to the information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holding in Drafting-division pending printed materials
rubrics_metrics.description: The file is sent to the Drafting-division, where it is held until the specification (printed) is received from the Public Printer and the printed drawing from the photolithographer. The class to which the case belongs is noted ... and the file and 'bond-copies' of specification and drawing are sent to the File-room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Bond-copies' are printed on bond-paper and bound with the patent-head.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binding and sealing of patent
rubrics_metrics.description: There the specification and drawing, with the patent-head previously received from the Issue-division, are bound, the seal-paper pasted on, and the case returned to the Issue-division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Here all the papers are finally compared with the Patent-Head Book, and it is seen that the different parts agree and are correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official signature and sealing
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent, being ready for the official signatures and seal, is sent to the Commissioner. The patent is signed by the Secretary of the Interior and the Commissioner of Patents, and the seal of the Office is affixed thereunto.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packaging, addressing, and dispatch procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: It is then sent to the File-room and placed in an envelope bearing ... the number and name corresponding to the number of the patent and name of the inventor. The envelope containing the patent-papers, with the file belonging to the case, is again sent over to the Issue-division. The patent is addressed to the proper party, and the time the patent is sent out is noted on the Alphabetical Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previous to the addressing of the patent the file is compared with the register, to see if any change has been made in the address of the person to whom the patent is to be sent, and such change, if any, is properly noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification records entry
rubrics_metrics.description: The case is now entered on the 'Classification Records,' kept in the Issue-division, the data for this entry being taken from the file, and the file is returned to the file-room, where it is retained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling informal drawings admitted for examination only
rubrics_metrics.description: If a drawing has been admitted for examination only, and is informal when it reaches the draftsman's desk ... both the file and drawing are here stopped, and the party in interest notified of the fact. When the drawing has been corrected the case is returned to the Examiner, and is started on its course to issue de novo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent-head preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent-heads are made up in the Issue-division from the Patent-Head Book ... As soon as the patent-head is completed it is sent to the File-room for the action indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making lists for internal publications and divisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The necessary lists for the Gazette, the draftsman, machinist, and Record-room, &c., are made up in the Issue-division, the data being obtained from the Patent-Head Book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement of brief for Gazette publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief taken from the file ... is sent to the Gazette-division, and is there arranged for publication in that journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing photolithography and proof approval workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawing obtained from the Drafting-division ... has the proper name, title, and number printed upon it by the printer in the Patent Office building, and is sent to the photolithographer, who returns it with a proof-sheet to the Chief Draftsman. After the proof of the drawing is passed upon and approved, it is sent back to the photolithographer, and the original drawing is held for the action indicated elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery of printed specs/drawings to Specification-division
rubrics_metrics.description: The specifications and drawings, when printed by the Public Printer and photolithographer, are delivered in the Specification-division, and the bond-copies are sent to the Chief Draftsman, who receives them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model identification and public display
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawing having been a second time sent to the photolithographer for the production of copies (library size), is afterward sent to the Model-room for identification of the model, which is then exposed to the public in its appropriate case, and the drawing returned to the Drafting-division to be deposited in its proper portfolio.
